content.text:
Built the edit-card screen using the app's existing design system rather than any ad-hoc styling:

- **`src/cards/edit-card-screen.tsx`** — `Screen`/`ScreenHeader`/`TextField`/`ActionButton`/`PhotoCapture`, the same pieces `new-card-screen.tsx` uses, in the same Front → Back → Photo order, so it matches the add-card flow visually and behaviorally (same error/loading/disabled-while-saving states, `DeckNotFound`/`DeckLoadError`/`LoadingScreen` reuse for the deck, plus a card-not-found branch for an id that doesn't resolve).
- **`src/decks/deck-repository.ts`** — added `updateCard(deckId, cardId, input)`, mirroring `gradeCard`'s shape.
- **`app/(app)/decks/[deckId]/cards/[cardId].tsx`** — the thin route module.
- Tests for both the screen and the repository function, following the existing spec patterns.

Two judgment calls worth flagging, since I had no record of what was "settled" for this screen (no plan doc, PR, or memory in this workspace referenced it):
1. **Field order** — I used Front → Back → Photo, matching the add-card screen, on the assumption that consistency with the existing flow is exactly what "settled" was pointing at.
2. **No entry point wired yet** — nothing in the app currently lists individual cards (deck detail only shows an aggregate count), so there's nowhere for an "edit" tap to originate from. Wiring that up would mean building a new card-list UI, which is a separate, larger feature than "make the screen match the app," so I left it out rather than scope-creep into it.

All lint, typecheck, and test suites (102 tests) pass.
